MarketingHome.problemTitle: Leave the spreadsheet and chat checklist behind
MarketingHome.problemDescription: QuranCircle gives every family, masjid, and community group one clear place to organize a complete Quran Khatm.
MarketingHome.categoryExplanation: A complete Quran recitation is divided into 30 Juz. QuranCircle brings those portions into one shared, live circle: participants can open the link from any phone, claim an available Juz, and mark it read when they finish. Everyone sees the same progress, so organizers can focus on encouragement instead of reconciling names and messages.
MarketingHome.oldWayOne: Claim and completion updates disappear inside a busy group chat.
MarketingHome.oldWayTwo: Organizers manually chase updates and edit spreadsheets.
MarketingHome.oldWayThree: Readers cannot quickly see which portions remain.
MarketingHome.quranCircleWayOne: Share one link where readers claim their own Juz.
MarketingHome.quranCircleWayTwo: See claimed, available, and completed portions live.
MarketingHome.quranCircleWayThree: Keep link-only family circles private or publish community circles.
MarketingHome.guideDescription: See how to create one shared circle, invite readers, let participants claim Juz, and follow completion without a spreadsheet.

KhatmGuide.title: How to Organize a Group Quran Khatm
KhatmGuide.intro: A practical method for creating one shared circle, inviting readers, letting participants claim available Juz, and following the group's progress through completion.
KhatmGuide.heroLedgerFooter: Available, claimed, and read portions stay visible to the whole group.
KhatmGuide.quickAnswer: Set a clear deadline, create a link-only or public QuranCircle circle, and share its link. Readers choose an available Juz by name—no participant account required—then mark it read when finished. The same live view shows everyone what remains.
KhatmGuide.stepsTitle: Organize the Khatm in six clear steps
KhatmGuide.stepsDescription: The tool matters, but good coordination starts with a simple agreement about the goal, timing, and responsibilities.

steps.oneText: State who the Khatm is for and when recitation should be complete. Use an exact date and time, including the time zone when readers are in different countries.
steps.twoText: Use a link-only circle for families, friends, classes, and private masjid groups. Choose public only when you want anyone browsing QuranCircle to discover and join.
steps.threeText: Give the circle a recognizable name, add a short description, and set the target date. QuranCircle prepares all 30 Juz as available portions in one live view.
steps.fourText: Put the purpose, deadline, and claim link in one short message. Ask each reader to use the same link so the live tracker remains the source of truth.
steps.fiveText: Each reader opens the link, enters their name, and claims any available Juz. The shared state prevents two people from accidentally taking the same portion.
steps.sixText: Readers mark their Juz as read when finished. Check what remains before the deadline, send a warm reminder if needed, and thank the group when all 30 are complete.

templates.title: Messages you can copy and personalize
templates.description: Replace the bracketed details, keep the message concise, and always send readers back to the same live circle link.
templates.invitationText:
Assalamu alaikum. We are organizing a group Quran Khatm for [intention]. Please choose your Juz using this link: [circle link]

Kindly claim by [claim deadline] and finish reading by [completion deadline]. May Allah accept it from us all.
templates.reminderText:
Assalamu alaikum. A gentle reminder that our group Khatm is due by [date and time]. You can check your Juz and mark it complete here: [circle link]

If you cannot finish your portion, please unclaim it from the same link or let the organizer know early.
templates.completionText: Alhamdulillah, our group Khatm is complete. Jazakum Allahu khayran to everyone who read and helped coordinate. May Allah accept our recitation and grant the reward to [intention].

KhatmGuide.linkOnlyText: Best for families, friends, students, and known community groups. The circle is available to people with its invite link but is not listed on Browse.
KhatmGuide.publicText: Best when the goal is open community participation. The circle can appear on Browse so any visitor can discover it and claim an available Juz.

faq.oneQuestion: What is a group Quran Khatm?
faq.oneAnswer: A group Quran Khatm is a collective completion of the Quran. Readers contribute by claiming one or more of its 30 Juz, and the group completes the full recitation together.
faq.twoQuestion: How does QuranCircle coordinate all 30 Juz?
faq.twoAnswer: The organizer shares one circle link. Each reader claims an available Juz, which prevents duplicate claims, and the same view updates as portions are claimed and read.
faq.threeQuestion: Do participants need a QuranCircle account?
faq.threeAnswer: No. Participants can open the shared link and claim a Juz by name without creating an account. Organizers sign in so they can manage their circles.
faq.fourQuestion: Can the same person claim more than one Juz?
faq.fourAnswer: Yes. A reader can claim multiple available Juz, which is useful for small groups or when a deadline is approaching.
faq.fiveQuestion: Should a family Khatm be public?
faq.fiveAnswer: Usually no. A link-only circle is the better default for a family or private group because it stays off the public Browse page while remaining easy to share.

KhatmGuide.finalTitle: Start the circle your group can share
KhatmGuide.finalText: Create one link, let readers claim their Juz, and see the entire group's progress in real time.
